_metadata.generated_by: refrag spectral_retrieval pipeline run, identical pipeline_id (od_spectral_retrieval_pipeline) on both domains; only the input scalar series differs
_metadata.comparability_note: Same orchestrator, same operators, same query/task config. Inputs are 1D floats either way: markets feeds log_returns from price bins, quantum feeds Re(rho[t,0,0]) from density matrices. Resulting operator_coefficient embeddings live in the same coordinate system, making cross-domain spectral_similarity meaningful.

finding.headline: Markets (financial) and Quantum (spin-boson) trajectories both saturate the pipeline's 11-node FAISS retrieval cap, but at different edge counts and very different validity_probability regimes. The (n_nodes, n_edges) signature labels do NOT overlap, so cross-domain transfer must be found in the operator_coefficients embedding space, not in the signature labels themselves.

markets.scalar_projection_note: 1-second bin closes -> log returns. Sliced per oracle winner trade [entry_ts, exit_ts].
markets.natural_taxonomy_interpretation: Monotonic: more nodes/edges = longer hold = higher net_bps. (11, 53) is the saturated long-hold class. Minority classes are the finer-structure short-horizon classes.

quantum_spin_boson.scalar_projection_note: Re(rho[t, 0, 0]) per timestep from 2x2 density matrix trajectories.
quantum_spin_boson.natural_taxonomy_interpretation: Binary: weak/moderate coupling (lambda<=200) vs strong coupling (lambda=500). Coupling regime is the deterministic discriminator; temperature regime (Tavg 77-500) and initial state (exc/sup) do not introduce new signatures.

cross_domain_observations.name: 11-node saturation is shared
cross_domain_observations.claim: Both domains saturate at exactly n_nodes=11. This is the FAISS retrieval top_k cap of the spectral_retrieval pipeline, not a property of either domain.
cross_domain_observations.implication: The pipeline's dominant 'saturation regime' is a STRUCTURAL property of refrag, not of markets or quantum. Cross-domain comparison inside the saturated band is valid.

cross_domain_observations.name: Edge-count regimes differ
cross_domain_observations.claim: Markets saturates at 53 edges; Quantum saturates at 45-46 edges. Both have the same 11 nodes, so Markets' retrieved chunks have substantially denser cross-chunk relationships than Quantum's.
cross_domain_observations.implication: Either Markets' price-bin log returns generate richer spectral overlap between adjacent windows than density-matrix populations do, OR the evidence_graph_builder is finding domain-specific edge types in one set that don't exist in the other. Worth a follow-up that inspects edge metadata, not just counts.

cross_domain_observations.name: Validity probability regimes differ by ~2.7x
cross_domain_observations.claim: Markets vp ~0.31 mean; Quantum vp ~0.85 mean. Tight stdev within each domain (~0.024 / ~0.027).
cross_domain_observations.implication: The operator_validity_posterior is judging Quantum trajectories as much more 'valid' than Markets trajectories. Either quantum signal is genuinely cleaner (controlled physics, no measurement noise), or the validity scoring depends on a property that quantum dynamics satisfy more readily (e.g., spectral coherence, stationarity).

cross_domain_observations.name: Signatures do not overlap directly
cross_domain_observations.claim: No (n_nodes, n_edges) signature appears in BOTH domains' outputs.
cross_domain_observations.implication: Cross-domain transfer cannot be detected via signature-label matching. It must be detected via spectral_similarity on the operator_coefficients vectors (which live in the same embedding space because both runs used the same pipeline).

cross_domain_observations.name: Retrieval policy is degenerate
cross_domain_observations.claim: 100% of trajectories in BOTH domains selected `spectral_target` mode (vs available alternatives candidate_similarity / hybrid).
cross_domain_observations.implication: The retrieval_policy_learner is not exploring. This is consistent across runs and probably means the policy has collapsed to one mode. Worth investigating whether exploration_policy_controller is producing meaningful gap signals.

open_question_for_next_run.question: Can the cross_domain_transfer_detector in spectral_similarity mode find Markets winners whose operator_coefficients fingerprint matches lambda=500 quantum trajectories more than they match lambda<=200 quantum trajectories?
open_question_for_next_run.why_it_matters: If yes: the embedding space carries domain-specific physical-regime information that survives saturation. The cross-domain bridge is real, even though the signature labels don't overlap.
open_question_for_next_run.command: from refrag_discovery.control_plane.cross_domain_transfer_detector import detect_cross_domain_transfer; detect_cross_domain_transfer(source_domain='markets', target_domain='quantum', comparison_mode='spectral_similarity', similarity_threshold=0.7)
